comparison: Perfect agreement on RSC hopping vs ISW2 sliding mechanisms (C3, C14-C18). Both evaluations find the salt-sensitivity data and diffusion measurements compelling. OpenEval additionally includes C19 (nucleotide effects on RSC diffusion) which peer reviewers address separately in R8.

Complete agreement on remodeler collision dynamics (C21-C26). Both evaluations accept the quantitative measurements, three collision types, and scanning speed calculations. Peer review describes this as an 'elegant two-color assay' while OpenEval emphasizes validation through simulation analysis.

Full agreement on nucleosome barrier effects and sequestration (C4, C27-C29). Both evaluations accept the differential ATP-dependent behavior between RSC and ISW2, with peer reviewers noting nucleosomes 'repel or sequester' remodelers and OpenEval emphasizing the ATP-dependent binding turnover interpretation.

Strong agreement on nucleosome translocation characterization (C5, C30-C39). Both find the processivity and speed measurements compelling. OpenEval explicitly notes the caveat about 5 pN tension (C70) potentially enhancing processivity, while peer reviewers accept the methodology without raising this concern.

Divergent confidence levels on directional bias claims (C42-C44, C71-C72, C74). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to small sample sizes (25 RSC, 21 ISW2 events) and experimental caveats, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED and emphasize 'fundamentally important implications.' Both acknowledge the authors' statement that more data are needed.

Agreement on methodological advance (C49) comparing current long-range measurements to prior short-range studies. OpenEval groups this with histone retention and gel assay claims (C50, C62-C63), while peer reviewers address C49 separately as a fundamental advance in single-molecule microscopy.

Overlap on histone retention during translocation (C50). OpenEval groups C50 with comparison to prior work (C49) and gel assays (C62-C63), while peer reviewers focus specifically on histone retention with caveats about Nap1 absence (C50-C52). Both accept the observation as valid.

Agreement on translocation frequency calculations (C40-C41). Peer reviewers describe this as part of 'rigorous quantitative analysis' while OpenEval emphasizes the integration of data from multiple figures. OpenEval additionally includes C45 (contextualizing rapid 1D search) which peer reviewers address in R12.

Agreement on background literature claims (C1-C2, C6-C13, C20). Both evaluations accept these as accurate characterizations of prior work providing essential context. Peer reviewers group these with additional literature claims (C46-C48, C53-C57, C68) that OpenEval addresses separately in R9.

Agreement on contextual literature citations (C46-C48, C51-C57, C68). OpenEval groups these as mechanistic context from prior structural and biochemical studies, while peer reviewers combine them with introductory background claims. Both find the citations accurate and interpretations reasonable.

Strong agreement on experimental methodology (C58-C61, C64-C66, C69-C70). Both evaluations accept the methods as sound with appropriate caveats. OpenEval emphasizes the acknowledged limitations (tension, Nap1 absence, localization precision), while peer reviewers praise 'well-conducted experiments' and 'fundamental single-molecule microscopy.'

Agreement on speculative claims (C67, C73) about in vivo implications. Both evaluations accept these as appropriately qualified hypotheses requiring validation. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN emphasizing they remain untested, while peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED noting they 'will undoubtedly spark exciting future research.'

Minor overlap on C19 (nucleotide effects on RSC diffusion). OpenEval includes this with main diffusion mechanism claims (R1), while peer reviewers address it separately as part of comprehensive diffusion characterization. Both accept the finding without challenge.

Minor overlap on C45 (contextualizing rapid 1D search relative to in vivo residence times). OpenEval groups this with translocation frequency calculations (R7) as logical inference, while peer reviewers include it with speculative interpretations (R12) about future research directions.

Minor overlap on gel assay validation (C62-C63). OpenEval includes these with histone retention and speed comparison claims (R6), while peer reviewers group them with broader methodological claims (R10). Both accept the validation data without question.

Minor overlap on RSC eviction activity context (C51-C52). OpenEval includes these as part of broader literature context (R9), while peer reviewers group them with histone retention observations (R7). Both accept the surprising nature of histone retention given RSC's known eviction activity.

Minor overlap on C69 (methodological caveat). OpenEval includes this with comprehensive methodology claims (R10), while peer reviewers group it with speculative interpretations (R12). Both accept the caveat as appropriately acknowledged.
